items.title: Top fund manager warns most software firms won't survive AI

featured_image.name: Fund Beating 99% of Peers Sees Few Software Firms Surviving ...

items.description:
A fund manager whose portfolio has outperformed 99% of competitors is sounding the alarm on software stocks, warning that artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to the industry and that only a handful of companies will survive the coming disruption.

"We think application software faces an existential threat from AI," said Nick Evans, whose $12 billion global technology fund at Polar Capital beat 99% of peers over the past year and 97% over five years, in comments reported by Bloomberg on Sunday.[1]

The warning comes as software stocks have suffered a brutal start to 2026. An exchange-traded fund tracking the U.S. software sector has plummeted more than 21% this year, according to data from S3 Partners, while hedge funds have generated $24 billion in profits by betting against the sector. The software industry has seen roughly $1 trillion wiped from its market capitalization since late January, sparked by fears that AI large language models could disintermediate traditional enterprise applications.[2][3][4]

items.title: EU's Kallas rejects US criticism, urges Europe to 'reclaim agency'

featured_image.name: Kaja Kallas attends Munich Security Conference | News | ERR

items.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference concluded Sunday with European leaders sending a clear message: the continent must take greater responsibility for its own defense amid shifting transatlantic dynamics. Over three days of discussions, top officials outlined plans for increased military spending, nuclear deterrence cooperation, and reduced dependence on Washington.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas rejected American criticism of Europe, pushing back against suggestions that "woke and decadent Europe" faces "civilizational erasure." Speaking at the conference's closing session, Kallas outlined three priorities: defending Europe starting with Ukraine, securing the neighborhood through EU enlargement, and building global partnerships. She warned that Russia "must not gain more at the negotiating table than it has achieved on the battlefield."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russia offers to halt strikes if Ukraine holds elections

featured_image.name: Russia revives election-day truce offer, proposes UN rule for Ukraine

items.description:
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin announced Saturday that Moscow is prepared to suspend airstrikes on election day if Ukraine holds presidential polls, reiterating an earlier offer from President Vladimir Putin while questioning the legitimacy of President Volodymyr Zelensky's government.

The announcement comes days before a new round of trilateral talks between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine scheduled for February 17-18 in Geneva, and as Washington continues pressing Kyiv to hold elections as a condition for U.S. security guarantees.

items.title: Rubio backs Orban reelection bid during Hungary visit

featured_image.name: Rubio meets Orbán in Budapest as US and Hungary are to sign ...

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to Budapest on Monday to meet with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban, signing a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement and delivering a strong endorsement of the embattled leader just weeks before Hungary's April 12 elections. Rubio told Orban that President Donald Trump is "deeply committed to your success" and that Orban's continued leadership is in America's national interest.[1][2]

The high-profile visit comes as Orban and his Fidesz party face their most difficult electoral challenge since retaking power in 2010. Opposition leader Peter Magyar's center-right Tisza party leads in most polls, with a recent Idea Institute survey showing Tisza at 48% among committed voters compared to 38% for Fidesz.[3]

items.title: India opens AI summit as first major Global South host

featured_image.name: Macron, Lula da Silva among 20 world leaders to attend upcoming ...

items.description:
India kicks off one of the largest artificial intelligence gatherings ever staged as Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates the India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Monday. The five-day event, running from February 16 to 20, is the first major global AI summit to be hosted in the Global South, positioning India as a central voice in shaping the future of the technology.[1][2][3]

The summit brings together approximately 20 heads of state and government, including French President Emmanuel Macron, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, along with ministerial delegations from over 45 countries. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and senior officials from multiple international organizations are also participating.[4][5][6]

items.title: ByteDance to add safeguards to Seedance 2.0 after Hollywood backlash

featured_image.name: Disney sends cease and desist letter to ByteDance over ...

items.description: The Walt Disney Company has accused ByteDance of large-scale intellectual property theft, sending a cease-and-desist letter to the Chinese tech giant over its newly launched AI video generator Seedance 2.0. The tool, released on Thursday, February 12, has drawn rapid condemnation from Hollywood studios and creative organizations, prompting ByteDance to pledge stronger safeguards.

items.title: Gold holds above $5,000 as stronger dollar, thin holiday trading weigh

featured_image.name: Gold and silver keep hitting record highs. But is the precious metals market 'broken'?

items.description:
Gold prices edged lower in early trading on Monday but held above the $5,000-per-ounce mark as a stronger dollar and profit-taking weighed on the precious metal following last week's inflation-driven rebound. Trading volumes remained thin with U.S. markets closed for Presidents Day and Chinese exchanges shut for Lunar New Year celebrations.[1][2][3]

Spot gold slipped 0.4% to around $5,020 per ounce in early Monday trading, according to The Business Times. The pullback came after the metal recovered from mid-week lows near $4,880 to close above $5,040 on Friday, buoyed by softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data.[4][5][6]

items.title: Iran proposes energy and mining deals ahead of Geneva talks

featured_image.name: Iran's Araghchi slams European powers for 'irrelevance' in nuclear ...

items.description:
Iran is seeking a nuclear agreement with the United States that would deliver economic benefits for both nations, an Iranian diplomat said Sunday, days before a second round of talks between Tehran and Washington scheduled for Tuesday in Geneva.

The discussions encompass potential business opportunities in oil and gas fields, mining investments, and even aircraft purchases, according to Hamid Ghanbari, deputy director for economic diplomacy at Iran's foreign ministry, as reported by the semi-official Fars news agency and wire service Reuters. Ghanbari argued that the 2015 nuclear pact with world powers had failed to secure American economic interests. "For the sake of an agreement's durability, it is essential that the U.S. also benefits in areas with high and quick economic returns," he said.[1][2][3]

items.title: Netanyahu demands Iran dismantle nuclear infrastructure in US deal

featured_image.name: Netanyahu on Iran — an assessment

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Sunday that any nuclear agreement between the United States and Iran must include the complete dismantling of Iran's nuclear infrastructure, not merely a pause on uranium enrichment. The demand comes ahead of a second round of US-Iran talks scheduled for Tuesday in Geneva.

Speaking at the Conference of Presidents of Major American Jewish Organizations' 51st Annual National Leadership Mission in Jerusalem, Netanyahu outlined specific conditions he conveyed to President Donald Trump during their White House meeting last week. "There shall be no enrichment capability — not stopping the enrichment process, but dismantling the equipment and the infrastructure that allows you to enrich in the first place," Netanyahu said, according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: Satellite images reveal China expanding nuclear sites in Sichuan

featured_image.name: Satellite images show China working on nuclear propulsion ...

items.description:
Satellite imagery has revealed rapid expansion at Chinese nuclear weapons facilities in Sichuan Province, signaling an accelerating effort to modernize Beijing's arsenal as global arms control frameworks weaken.

The images, first reported by The New York Times on Saturday, show construction activity at several secretive facilities built during the Cold War, including sites believed to be involved in producing plutonium cores for warheads and testing the high explosives needed to trigger nuclear detonations.[1][2][3]

The developments come just ten days after the New START treaty between the United States and Russia expired on February 5, leaving no binding limits on strategic nuclear weapons for the first time since 1972.[4][5]

items.title: Trump pledged support for Israeli strikes on Iran if talks fail

featured_image.name: Trump to Netanyahu: U.S. prefers deal with Iran to war, for now - Axios

items.description:
President Donald Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during their December meeting at Mar-a-Lago that the United States would support Israeli strikes on Iran's ballistic missile program if Washington's negotiations with Tehran collapse, according to CBS News, citing two sources familiar with the matter.[1][2]

The disclosure comes as a second round of nuclear talks between the U.S. and Iran is set to begin in Geneva next week, with a U.S. delegation including envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner scheduled to meet with Iranian officials on Tuesday.[3][4]

items.title: Ukrainian drone strike hits Russian Black Sea port before Geneva talks

featured_image.name: Ukraine drone strike hits Russian Black Sea port ahead of peace talks

items.description:
A Ukrainian drone strike set fires at Russia's Taman port in the Krasnodar region on Sunday, wounding two people and damaging oil infrastructure, as both sides prepare for US-brokered peace talks scheduled for this week in Geneva. The attack comes amid intensified diplomatic maneuvering and continued fighting ahead of the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24.

Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said an oil storage tank, warehouse, and terminals sustained damage in the village of Volna, where Taman port is located. More than 100 personnel were working to extinguish multiple fires at the site, he said in a Telegram post. Ukraine's military intelligence confirmed the overnight strike on the oil terminal.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump says Board of Peace nations pledge $5B for Gaza

featured_image.name: White House plans Gaza Board of Peace leaders meeting in D.C.

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that member states of his Board of Peace have pledged more than $5 billion for humanitarian and reconstruction efforts in Gaza, while also committing thousands of personnel to a UN-authorized stabilization force in the Palestinian territory.[1][2]

The announcement, made via Truth Social, comes ahead of the first formal gathering of the Board of Peace, scheduled for February 19 at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace in Washington, D.C.. Trump emphasized that Hamas must uphold its "commitment to full and immediate demilitarization" as part of the US-brokered ceasefire agreement.[2][3][4]

items.title: Russia investigates tanker crash at key Baltic oil port

featured_image.name: Tanker loads naphtha at Novatek's Ust-Luga terminal, data ...

items.description:
Russian authorities on Sunday launched an investigation into an incident involving an oil tanker at the Ust-Luga seaport, a key outlet for the nation's crude oil and fuel exports via the Baltic Sea. The collision, which occurred on Saturday, damaged port infrastructure but resulted in no injuries or petroleum spills.

According to the Northwestern Transport Prosecutor, the tanker Tony struck a berth wall while arriving at the port in the Leningrad region to load petroleum products. The collision damaged both the berth wall and a port crane at the facility, Reuters reported.[1][2]

"The incident damaged the berth wall and the port crane. There were no injuries, and no petroleum spill occurred," the prosecutor said in a statement posted on Telegram.[2]

items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 docks at ISS after medical evacuation cut short previous mission

featured_image.name: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Secured in Spacecraft

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission docked at the International Space Station on Saturday, bringing the orbital laboratory back to its full seven-person complement following an unprecedented medical evacuation that cut short the previous crew's stay.

The Dragon spacecraft Freedom linked up with the station's Harmony module at approximately 3:15 p.m. EST, capping a 34-hour journey that began with a predawn launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Friday. The mission marks NASA's twelfth operational crew rotation under its Commercial Crew Program with SpaceX.[1][2]

items.title: UK and allies say Navalny was killed with rare dart frog toxin

featured_image.name: UK, allies say they're convinced Kremlin critic Navalny was poisoned

items.description:
Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned with epibatidine, a lethal toxin found in South American poison dart frogs, according to a joint announcement by five European nations on the second anniversary of his death in a Siberian penal colony.

The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands issued a joint statement on Saturday confirming that analyses of samples from Navalny "conclusively confirmed the presence of epibatidine," a substance not found naturally in Russia. The announcement, made at the Munich Security Conference, directly implicates the Russian government in Navalny's death, with the coalition stating that "only the Russian state had the combined means, motive and disregard for international law" to carry out the attack.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rubio urges transatlantic unity as Europe stresses self-reliance

featured_image.name: In Munich, Rubio urges transatlantic unity but lashes Europe on migration

items.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference opened this weekend to a fractured Western alliance, with European leaders delivering pointed assessments of transatlantic relations while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attempted to reassure anxious allies that Washington still values its oldest partnerships.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz set the tone on Friday when he declared that the rules-based world order "no longer exists" and acknowledged that "a deep divide has opened between Europe and the United States." Speaking directly to the American delegation, Merz warned that U.S. claims to global leadership have been "challenged, and possibly lost," while urging Europe to stop denying the scale of the geopolitical challenge it faces.[1][2]

items.title: Iran arrests over 50,000 in dragnet after deadly protest crackdown

featured_image.name: Arrests of protestors continue to roil Iran weeks after ...

items.description:
Iranian security forces have arrested more than 50,000 people in a sweeping campaign following a brutal crackdown last month that killed thousands of demonstrators, according to human rights groups. The dragnet, spanning major cities and rural towns, has targeted protesters, doctors, lawyers, students, actors, and reformist political figures, with many held incommunicado for days or weeks.[1][2]

The Associated Press reported that security agents have conducted late-night raids on homes and workplaces across the country, using surveillance footage and facial recognition technology to track down individuals who participated in protests that peaked in early January.[2][3]

items.title: NASA reviews Artemis II test data as moon mission eyes March

featured_image.name: More trouble for Artemis-II rocket, Moon launch likely delayed again

items.description:
NASA engineers are analyzing data from a confidence test conducted on February 12 as the agency works toward returning humans to the Moon for the first time in more than five decades. The test was designed to evaluate repairs made following a hydrogen leak that forced NASA to push back the Artemis II launch from its original February window.

During the test at Kennedy Space Center, operators partially filled the Space Launch System core stage liquid hydrogen tank to assess newly replaced seals in the propellant fueling area, NASA said in a statement. Teams encountered an issue with ground support equipment that reduced the flow of liquid hydrogen into the rocket, though engineers were able to achieve several key objectives and collect data at the same point in testing where a leak had been detected during the previous wet dress rehearsal.[1][2]

items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 to dock with ISS on Valentine's Day

featured_image.name: NASA and SpaceX set to launch Crew-12 to the ISS on Feb 13 ...

items.description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off early Friday morning carrying four astronauts toward the International Space Station, marking the 12th operational crew rotation mission under NASA's Commercial Crew Program. The Crew Dragon capsule "Freedom" is set to dock with the orbiting outpost this afternoon, delivering a relief crew after an unprecedented medical evacuation last month left the station short-staffed.

The mission launched at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, serving as commander, and Jack Hathaway as pilot, along with mission specialists Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos.[1][2][3]
